searchText: I've done another round of interop testing with 4 clients. The network started forking after 706 slots and lost finalization after 1186. I think the trigger might be insufficient resources on a single machine (slow proof computation), but it's good to see some clients able to recover. I haven't looked at the logs yet, but I've attached them on this page if anyone has time https://hackmd.io/@jimmygchen/r1m3moJ60 Yeah I think that makes sense. ignore this one, I'm going to try it again, kurtosis dump didn't capture full lighthouse logs 🤦‍♂️ ^ i can give it a shot against kubernetes, we wont see resource issues that easily then 🙂 there is a bug i have just found in lodestar to in storing and fetching when storing <128 columns that i am hunting down (and hence will give incorrect results) could be the reason for lodestar forking off Could you please shortly explain what are the benefits of having `CUSTODY_REQUIREMENT < SAMPLES_PER_SLOT` now? From my perspective it doesn't affect the network traffic: a peer would still subscribe to `SAMPLES_PER_SLOT` subnets. It would just decrease storage requirements It will allow clients who can, the ability to sample for data columns rather than subscribe to them. ex: custody = 4 and samples = 16 , you wouldn't need to subscribe to 12 other subnets. Without peer sampling as in the spec right now, there is no difference with custody=16. But peer sampling will be added back in the near future as an option from what I understand. Also primary reason to have custody requirement is for a stable backbone rather then to assert data availability of a block Not a resource limit issue 😄 network spontaneously combusts after like 11 epochs indeed this is on kubernetes, with a relatively low chance of any resource limits being hit (Atleast as defined in the kurtosis config here https://hackmd.io/@jimmygchen/r1m3moJ60) But there are obvious downsides of this solution: weaker backbones, harder to find peers for sync. Do we really need to adopt this prior to future changes? Any future change will always involve us in reducing the number of subnets participated in. Ex: 16 -> 4 . This just allows us to do so without a hardfork The alternative is that if we want to finally run with peer sampling, we will need a hardfork to do it because you can't just drop down the number of custodied subnets without being penalized For missed blocks about Prysm full node, we have an issue I'm currently working on: As soon as we have a fork, then the prysm full node will take a very long time to process incoming blocks. It will always lag and so will be unable to propose blocks. (It does not happen with Prysm super nodes.) So does it makes sense until the future soft-fork make the `custody_subnet_count >= SAMPLES_PER_SLOT` the recommended (or obligatory) option for all clients? if you do this, you would need a hardfork to make `custody_subnet_count < SAMPLES_PER_SLOT` its not optional if older nodes start penalizing you and banning you for having a lower custody count fixed the bug, but i also see another issue prsym seems to be requesting columns not custodied Do you have an image/kurtosis config so I can reproduce locally? excerpts.author: nashatyrev
excerpts.content:
Could you please shortly explain what are the benefits of having `CUSTODY_REQUIREMENT < SAMPLES_PER_SLOT` now? 
From my perspective it doesn't affect the network traffic: a peer would still subscribe to `SAMPLES_PER_SLOT` subnets. It would just decrease storage requirements

excerpts.author: nishant0
excerpts.content:
It will allow clients who can, the ability to sample for data columns rather than subscribe to them. ex: custody = 4 and samples = 16 , you wouldn't need to subscribe to 12 other subnets. Without peer sampling as in the spec right now, there is no difference with custody=16.  But peer sampling will be added back in the near future as an option from what I understand. 

Also primary reason to have custody requirement is for a stable backbone rather then to assert data availability of a block

excerpts.author: nashatyrev
excerpts.content: But there are obvious downsides of this solution: weaker backbones, harder to find peers for sync. Do we really need to adopt this prior to future changes?

excerpts.author: nishant0
excerpts.content: Any future change will always involve us in reducing the number of subnets participated in. Ex: 16 -> 4 . This just allows us to do so without a hardfork

excerpts.author: nishant0
excerpts.content: The alternative is that if we want to finally run with peer sampling, we will need a hardfork to do it because you can't just drop down the number of custodied subnets without being penalized

excerpts.author: manunlp
excerpts.content:
For missed blocks about Prysm full node, we have an issue I'm currently working on:
As soon as we have a fork, then the prysm full node will take a very long time to process incoming blocks.
It will always lag and so will be unable to propose blocks. (It does not happen with Prysm super nodes.)

excerpts.author: nashatyrev
excerpts.content: So does it makes sense until the future soft-fork make the  `custody_subnet_count >= SAMPLES_PER_SLOT`  the recommended (or obligatory) option for all clients?

excerpts.author: nishant0
excerpts.content: if you do this, you would need a hardfork to make `custody_subnet_count < SAMPLES_PER_SLOT`

excerpts.author: nishant0
excerpts.content: its not optional if older nodes start penalizing you and banning you for having a lower custody count
